content: Tung Wah Hospital, known in Chinese as 東華醫院, is a hospital located in Hong Kong and operates under the Tung Wah Group of Hospitals. It is situated above Possession Point in Sheung Wan and holds the distinction of being the first hospital established in Colonial Hong Kong for the general public during the 1870s. The hospital's construction was officially declared on March 26, 1870, under the Tung Wah Hospital Incorporation Ordinance. The initiative to build the hospital arose after the Registrar General of the British Colony observed a distressing situation where the dead and dying were indiscriminately placed together in a temple. This dire need for a proper medical facility was further exacerbated by the arrival of the Third Pandemic of bubonic plague from China. Although the hospital was not officially established until 1872, its construction was subsidized by the government with a grant of HKD $45,000 and an additional HKD $15,000 in land allocation. The hospital's grand opening on February 14, 1872, was considered one of the most significant events in Colonial Hong Kong's history. At the time, cultural prejudices posed significant challenges. Many Chinese citizens harbored distrust toward Western medicine and practices, including surgery, and some even preferred death over seeking treatment in a Western clinic. To address the growing population in Kowloon and the New Territories, the government enacted Ordinance No. 38, known as the 1911 Expansion of Tung Wah Hospital Ordinance, in 1911. This ordinance facilitated the hospital's expansion in conjunction with Kwong Wah Hospital. Currently, Tung Wah Hospital has a capacity of 633 beds, including 494 for in-patients, 93 for day patients, and 46 for rehabilitation day placements. It is the second-largest general hospital within the Hong Kong West Cluster. The Main Block of Tung Wah Hospital is classified as a Grade III historic building. The hospital is affiliated with the Li Ka Shing Faculty of Medicine, and the University of Hong Kong provides clinical attachment opportunities for its medical students.
